issues.description: The template implementation of GroverMultiQubitWithAuxiliaryQubit's simulate() is annotated to return a statevector (list[complex]) but the problem statement and the solution expect/return measurement counts (a dictionary of bitstring->counts). This mismatch between the template type hint and the expected behavior (counts) can confuse students about whether to produce a statevector or measurement histogram and may lead to incorrect implementations or type errors when tests expect counts.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template simulate() annotation and docstring to match the exercise description and the solution: have simulate() return a dict[str, int] (measurement counts). Also update the template implementation guidance to recommend using a qasm simulator (or run shots on an appropriate simulator) so that get_counts() returns meaningful results, or if a statevector is desired, adjust the problem statement to explicitly request a statevector.
